prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"An API reference table for scanning REST endpoints and quickly comparing their method, auth requirement, rate limit, and behavior.","reading":"Readers anchor on the endpoint path, then scan the short Method/Auth/Rate limit control fields, and finally read the Description for behavior. Rows must remain identifiable as units even when descriptions wrap.","groups":["Endpoint stands alone as the row identifier.","Method, Auth, and Rate limit form a compact control-metadata block; they are short categorical values read together.","Description is explanatory prose and should receive the remaining width for readable line lengths."],"keep_intact":["Endpoint paths, especially /api/v1/exports/{jobId}/download","HTTP methods such as DELETE","Auth values such as Bearer and Admin","Rate values such as 600/min","Description words and identifiers should not be split mid-token"],"may_wrap":["Description prose across several lines","The 'Rate limit' header between words if necessary","Other short headers only as a last resort"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [300, 76, 67, 89, 187] · table 720×485px · row heights [36, 129, 129, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [294, 76, 67, 89, 193] · table 720×461px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [308, 76, 67, 89, 179] · table 720×485px · row heights [36, 129, 129, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
